stem: What is the primary mechanism behind Alloimmune Neonatal Neutropenia?

options.text: A genetic mutation inherited from both parents that stops neutrophil production.
Maternal antibodies attacking paternal antigens on the infant's neutrophils.
The infant's own immune system mistakenly attacking its bone marrow.
A toxic reaction to drugs administered during the labor process.

explanation: This occurs when the mother produces antibodies against antigens the baby inherited from the father, leading to transient destruction of the baby's white cells.
rationale: Focus on the interaction between maternal immune components and inherited paternal markers.

optionExplanations.A: This describes an autosomal recessive congenital condition, not an immune-mediated destruction problem.
optionExplanations.B: This occurs when the mother produces antibodies against antigens the baby inherited from the father, leading to transient destruction of the baby's white cells.
optionExplanations.C: This describes an autoimmune process within the infant, whereas alloimmune involves external antibodies from the mother.
optionExplanations.D: While drugs can cause neutropenia, the alloimmune variety is specifically defined by the interaction between maternal antibodies and fetal antigens.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Maternal antibodies attacking paternal antigens on the infant's neutrophils.
